verdict: Tight, well-sourced and properly labelled, but fix the ambiguous 'His', break two breathless runs with pauses, and give Nebius and DataVolt a few words each before we record.

defects.rule: Pronoun whose referent could be two different things
defects.quote: His ambition, as he told CNBC

defects.rule: A sentence carrying three or more figures
Unfamiliar company name with no few-word explanation
defects.quote: Nebius signed a preliminary framework for up to 50 megawatts

defects.rule: Unfamiliar company name with no few-word explanation
defects.quote: DataVolt plans a 1.5 gigawatt AI campus at Oxagon

defects.rule: More than 60 spoken words with no [Pause]
defects.quote: And Fortune says Amin is preparing for a stock market listing

defects.rule: More than 60 spoken words with no [Pause]
defects.quote: So when you read the next big gigawatt headline

worst_three.problem: The line before names both the Crown Prince and Tareq Amin, so listeners can't tell whose ambition this is, and could pin a corporate boast on the head of state.
worst_three.fix: Replace with: "Amin's ambition, as he told CNBC: 'We want to be the third-largest AI provider in the world, behind the United States and China.'"

worst_three.problem: About 64 words run from the IPO news straight into Wissam's personal view with no breath, so the switch from reported fact to opinion blurs on the ear.
worst_three.fix: Add [Pause] after "No timetable or size has been announced." and keep "This next part is my view, not a reported fact." as its own beat, followed by [Pause] before "After 25 years selling enterprise software..."

worst_three.problem: Four numbers in one breath (two countries, 2, 3, 2030) blur together on a phone speaker.
worst_three.fix: Split into two sentences: "S&P expects Saudi Arabia and the UAE to add two to three gigawatts between them. [Pause] That's by the end of the decade." Also explain the newcomers: "Nebius, a European AI cloud company, signed..." and "DataVolt, a Saudi data-centre developer, plans..."
